name: Kameari
tagline: Tokyo in 31 minutes and Otemachi in 35 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Katsushika City, served by JR Joban Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 35 minutes to Otemachi, 46 minutes to Shinjuku, 55 minutes to Shibuya and 46 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 1.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.7 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 1.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.6 m to 1.1 m, a difference of 1.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 9 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 5 to 10 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

groceries.name: イトーヨーカドー 亀有駅前店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 10 pharmacies. No facility recorded as a hospital lies within 2.5 km of the station. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: JR Joban Line.
congestion: JR Joban Line runs at 142% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三河島→日暮里, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000, 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000, 1LDK ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 2LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Kita-Ayase is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Kameari is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: About 2 km away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 4 minutes sooner than Kameari.

neighbours.lead: Kanamachi is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities, but Kameari is ahead on how easy the shopping is.

noiseSources: The nearest big road, 環七通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively many of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the JR Joban Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
